newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - China looks to S.Korea for diesel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - China looks to S.Korea for diesel.

text.p: China is turning to South Korea for its gas oil supplies for end-February and early March as prices in Singapore were still deemed too high despite recent large falls, traders said on Wednesday.
They said at least two 30,000-tonne spot cargoes were heard sold into China at around $200 per tonne cost-and-freight (c&f), $10 lower than the last cargo heard sold to China from this region.
Apart from spot cargoes, China also buys gas oil by term contracts from South Korea.

Traders said Korean refiners were willing to sell at a discount to Singapore spot quotes free-on-board (fob) basis, while refiners in Singapore are looking at around a 10-cent premium. A trader offered today at a 35-cent premium for early March lifting, fob.
A European major recently sold 5,000-10,000 tonnes of gas oil for mid-February lifting at $25.60 a barrel fob, traders said. But two cargo-sized deals were heard done at lower levels than that.
A Singapore trader sold 150,000 barrels of gas oil at $25.20 per barrel for Feb 24-28 lifting fob, while another local trader was said to have sold a cargo at $24.90 fob.
This was higher than the deal done on Tuesday at $24.80 a barrel fob.
Traders said despite tight jet fuel supplies, they think that current assessments for the jet fuel-gas oil spread at $6.00 a tonne was too wide. "It's an untenable situation," one trader said.
However, jet fuel continued to be bid at a firm level of $31.00 for 100,000 barrels, lifting Feb 20-24, 10 cents below Tuesday's bid.
Traders also said Thailand is seeking to sell second-half February jey fuel into Japan. Premiums to Japan are currently more than $2.00 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, c&f.
February gas oil swaps were weaker in early trading but recovered to $25.25/$25.35, five to 10 cents over Tuesday's quotes, with the jet fuel-gas oil regrade seen at $4.40/$4.80 a barrel.
